item.title: SEC regulatory agenda targets July 2026 for three crypto rulemakings (digital-asset offerings, broker-dealer custody, market structure)
item.category: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
item.description:
Per The Cryptonomist (July 11, 2026) citing the SEC's RegInfo Unified Agenda, the Securities and Exchange Commission has set July 2026 targets for three crypto rule proposals: (1) digital-asset offerings — a Division of Corporation Finance rulemaking that may include exemptions or safe harbors (legal authority listed as 'not yet determined'); (2) broker-dealer financial-responsibility, custody, and recordkeeping amendments (Rules 15c3-1, 15c3-3, 17a-3, 17a-4); and (3) market-structure amendments for crypto trading venues. As of July 11, 2026, no proposal had appeared in the Federal Register; the RegInfo entries reflect agenda-stage targets, not filed NPRMs. Corroborated by Decrypt, The Industry Spread, and Yahoo Finance.

item.title: GENIUS Act stablecoin rulemaking deadline (July 18, 2026) one week out — six agencies had not finalized implementing rules as of July 11
item.category: OCC / FDIC / NCUA / U.S. Treasury / FinCEN / OFAC
item.description:
As of July 11, 2026, six federal agencies — the OCC, FDIC, NCUA, U.S. Treasury, FinCEN, and OFAC — faced a statutory July 18, 2026 deadline (one year after the GENIUS Act's July 18, 2025 enactment) to finalize implementing rules for permitted payment stablecoin issuers (PPSIs), and had not yet issued final rules. Comment periods on the proposed rules closed by early June 2026. The proposed framework requires PPSIs to hold 1:1 reserves in cash, insured deposits, and short-term U.S. Treasuries, and treats issuers as financial institutions under the Bank Secrecy Act. Source: Tech Times (July 11, 2026); corroborated by CryptoSlate and rulemaking trackers (Chapman & Cutler, Paradigm).

item.title: First U.S. statutory ban on a Federal Reserve CBDC takes effect via the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R.6644 §1101)
item.category: U.S. Congress (21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, H.R.6644 §1101)
item.description:
On July 10, 2026, the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R.6644) became law without President Trump's signature. Per coverage by The Cryptonomist (July 10, 2026), corroborated by Tech Times (July 11, 2026) and CoinDesk (July 9-10, 2026), Section 1101 prohibits the Federal Reserve from issuing a central bank digital currency (CBDC) or any substantially similar digital asset through December 31, 2030. The bill passed the Senate 85-5 (June 22) and the House 358-32. Coverage reports a carve-out for open, permissionless, privately issued dollar-denominated digital assets (understood to include stablecoins). Statutory text cited by coverage but not independently retrieved. Follows the Senate-passage entry (2026-06-19-senate-passes-road-housing-cbdc-ban) and bill-text entry (2026-06-18-congress-cbdc-ban-road-to-housing-act).

item.title: OCC grants Circle final approval for a national trust bank charter (First National Digital Currency Bank, N.A. / Circle National Trust)
item.category: OCC (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency)
item.description:
On July 10, 2026, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency granted Circle Internet Group final approval to establish First National Digital Currency Bank, N.A. (operating as Circle National Trust), a national trust bank that will provide fiduciary digital-asset custody for Circle and its affiliates. Circle applied to the OCC on June 30, 2025 and received conditional approval in December 2025 before final approval on July 10, 2026. As reported, this is the first national trust bank charter granted to a stablecoin issuer. Source: Circle press release (July 10, 2026); corroborated by American Banker, CoinDesk, CNBC, and BusinessWire. OCC decision letter not independently retrieved.

item.title: Merged Senate CLARITY Act draft expected week of July 20; ethics provision remains the sticking point; no text filed as of July 9
item.category: U.S. Senate (Banking Committee / Agriculture Committee)
item.description:
CoinDesk reported (July 9, 2026) that a new merged version of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act — combining Senate Banking and Agriculture Committee texts, with reportedly more than 70 pages added — could be released as soon as the week of July 20, 2026 for potential Senate floor action. Per the reporting, the draft had not secured the Democratic support needed for 60 votes to clear a filibuster; the main open issue was an ethics provision restricting senior officials, including the president, from crypto business ties, with federal preemption rules and SEC/CFTC commissioner nominations also unresolved. No bill text had been filed as of July 9, 2026.

item.title: CFTC invokes emergency authority to stay KalshiEX's own rule change and orders fulfillment of Michigan-resident trades — first federal override targeting a DCM's state-court-directed rule amendment
item.category: CFTC (Commodity Futures Trading Commission)
item.description:
On July 14, 2026, the CFTC issued Press Release 9267-26, announcing it had exercised emergency authority under the Commodity Exchange Act to stay a KalshiEX rule change and order KalshiEX to fulfill pending trades. Background: a Michigan state court issued a temporary restraining order directing KalshiEX to cancel all executed trades by Michigan-resident customers; KalshiEX filed an emergency rule change with the CFTC to comply with that state court order. The CFTC stayed the KalshiEX rule change and ordered KalshiEX to fulfill all pending trades per normal exchange practices. CFTC Chairman Brian Quintenz Selig stated the action was 'unprecedented,' noting Michigan is 'the first state to attempt to directly interfere with already-executed transactions on a federally regulated exchange.' As of the release, the CFTC has filed preemption suits against nine states: Arizona, Connecticut, Illinois, Kentucky, Minnesota, New Mexico, New York, Rhode Island, and Wisconsin.
Primary source: CFTC Press Release 9267-26 (July 14, 2026) — https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9267-26

item.title: CLARITY Act: Senate staff expected to release unified crypto market-structure draft this week; floor vote targeted July 20; August 7 recess is the hard deadline — passage odds at 50%
item.category: U.S. Senate / Senate Banking & Agriculture Committees (via staff)
item.description:
Multiple credible outlets (crypto.news, TechTimes, The Hill) reported on July 11-12, 2026 that Senate staff are expected to release a unified draft of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (H.R. 3633) during the week of July 13, 2026, merging parallel Senate Banking and Agriculture Committee texts. Floor action is targeted for the week of July 20. The Senate leaves for its August recess on August 7, 2026, leaving approximately three working weeks. Galaxy Research has reduced 2026 passage odds to 50%, citing calendar compression, down from 60% earlier in July. Three disputes remain unresolved: (1) ethics/conflict-of-interest rules covering senior officials with crypto holdings; (2) CFTC commissioner vacancies; (3) Section 604 blockchain developer shield. H.R. 3633 passed the House 294-134 on July 17, 2025; cleared Senate Banking Committee 15-9 on May 14, 2026; placed on Senate Calendar No. 423 on June 1, 2026.

item.title: Arizona Department of Gaming serves cease-and-desist orders on five online gambling operators, alleging felony money laundering and gambling promotion
item.category: Arizona Department of Gaming
item.description:
On July 10, 2026, the Arizona Department of Gaming (ADG) issued cease-and-desist orders to BetOpenly, Bookmaker, Club WPT Online Poker, Kutt Inc., and Raffle Creator. Each order alleges three Arizona felonies under A.R.S. Title 13, Chapter 33: (1) promotion of gambling, (2) illegal control of an enterprise, and (3) money laundering. ADG additionally alleged underage gambling (under-21 access) at BetOpenly, Club WPT Online Poker, and Raffle Creator; commission-based peer-to-peer wagering (prohibited under Arizona social-gambling law) at BetOpenly and Kutt Inc.; and unlicensed horse racing, casino, and sports betting at Bookmaker; and online poker (illegal in Arizona) at Club WPT. All five are directed to immediately cease all gambling operations in Arizona. Future actions may include criminal charges, civil suits, restitution, and forfeiture. ADG Director Jackie Johnson stated: 'Arizona is taking decisive action against illegal gambling operators that put Arizonans at risk.' This action expands ADG's 2025 sweepstakes-casino enforcement pattern to peer-to-peer wagering platforms, offshore sportsbooks, and unlicensed poker operators.
Primary source: Arizona Department of Gaming — Press Release, July 10 2026 — https://gaming.az.gov/sites/default/files/July%2026_ADG%20Cease%20and%20Desist%20Orders_Press%20Release.pdf

item.title: North Carolina Governor Stein signs $34B SB 257 budget enacting 6% prediction-market tax on net trading-fee revenue, effective 2027
item.category: North Carolina Office of the Governor
item.description:
On July 8, 2026, North Carolina Governor Josh Stein signed Senate Bill 257, the state's approximately $34 billion fiscal year 2026 budget. As reported by GamblingNews (July 8, 2026), the enacted budget includes a 6% tax on the net trading fee revenue earned by prediction market operators with North Carolina users; platforms named in reporting include Kalshi and Polymarket. The tax is scheduled to take effect in 2027. The enacted budget does not impose state gambling licensing, know-your-customer, or responsible-gaming requirements on prediction-market platforms. This item supersedes the July 6 item (2026-07-06-north-carolina-prediction-market-tax), which covered SB 257 at conference committee stage; the Governor's signing converts it to enacted law.

item.title: New Jersey Senate Budget Committee approves amended S4447 (9% prediction-market gross income tax) 9-4; amended bill explicitly recognizes CFTC as federal regulator
item.category: New Jersey Senate Budget and Appropriations Committee
item.description:
As reported by GamblingNews (July 8, 2026), the New Jersey Senate Budget and Appropriations Committee approved amendments to S4447 by a 9-4 vote. The amended bill imposes a 9% tax on prediction market gross income for operators offering event contracts to New Jersey residents. The amended version explicitly recognizes the CFTC as the federal regulator of prediction markets and drops prior self-exclusion requirements. The New Jersey Office of Legislative Services estimated the tax would generate approximately $10.3 million to $15.3 million annually. The bill requires a full Senate vote, Assembly action, and the Governor's signature before becoming law.
